description:
Manki's air.2, Double Fist Slam, somersault version: his forward aerial. In the air he swings both arms up over his head and arches back like a drawn bow, then throws himself into one forward somersault, and the spin hurls both fists over the top together like a hammer: the two fists meet on his centre line well in front of him as his body pitches forward, and the somersault carries on round until he is upright again. The right fist carries the hitbox (a sphere about 0.5 m across), so where the right fist travels during the hit is the move. It launches the opponent up and away.

Who he is. Manki is a small, wiry pyromaniac monkey: big head, goggles, a tall spiky mane, a two-can spray jetpack on his back, a cocky grin. He moves like a scrappy cartoon brawler: fast, springy, everything thrown with his whole little body. Read him from behind: big clear silhouettes, the fists clearly above his head on the load and clearly in front of him on the hit.

How the game plays it. The match camera sits straight behind him, so the action must read from behind: the fists go up behind his head and come down through the middle, in front of his face, not off to one side. The game plays this 96-tick clip at about double speed. The fighter does not travel in the clip; the game moves him. Only the hips joint may translate, so turn the body about its middle (around the belly), not about the hips joint. The game crossfades in and out over about 0.1 s.

In the air. Tick 0 and tick 96 are his fall pose exactly (image 1). There is no floor contact.

Hands. From the gather (tick 10) to the end of the follow-through (tick 58) both hands are tight closed fists: all four fingers curled into the palm, the thumb closed outside across the index and middle fingers, never tucked inside the fingers and never sticking out. Use fist(). Keep the wrists close to the forearm line (under about 35 degrees): a hammer fist is a straight forearm with the little-finger side of the fist leading. Before tick 10 and after tick 58 the hands blend from and to the fall pose's relaxed half curl. Leave the fist deform, forearm offset and arm stretch helper joints at rest: no swelling, no stretch. The fists must stay visible: outside the mane and the head on the load, outside the belly, shorts and thigh holster on the hit. His head is big: the crown of the spiky mane is about 0.28 m above the Head joint, and the two jetpack cans stand behind his shoulders up to about 0.19 m above the Head joint. Fists pushed back behind his head land inside the mane or the cans, so on the load the fists go up over the crown, not back behind the head. The old version of this move buried both fists in the mane during the load and in his belly and thigh holster during the hit, with swollen fingers and wrists folded about 78 degrees; avoid all of that.

The move (96 ticks, played once):
- Tick 0: the fall pose.
- Tick 10, the gather: a small compression before the reach. The knees come up a little, the chest curls slightly over them, the chin tucks, both fists close and start to rise in front of his chest.
- Tick 22, the load builds: both arms swing up, fists together rising past his face to above his head, elbows bent and pointing out. The chest opens and starts arching back; the legs start swinging back behind him as a counterweight.
- Tick 31, full load (the tick before the hit): the drawn bow. His whole body is a backward C: chest arched back about 20-30 degrees; the arms nearly straight overhead (elbows only slightly bent), both fists close together just above and slightly behind the crown of his mane; the head pitched a little forward on the neck (chin down, eyes on the target) so the mane stays out of the fists' way; the knees bent with the shins and feet swung behind him. The hips have just started to tip forward, ahead of the chest: the somersault starts at the hips.
- Tick 35, over the top (the hit is already live): the whole body has pitched forward about 45 degrees into the somersault and the arms are whipping over with it, fists together above his forehead on the centre line, arms long; the knees start pulling up under him.
- Tick 39, the strike: the body has pitched forward about 90 degrees (lying face down in the air, his back toward the sky and the camera's view over it); the arms swing on past his head so both fists meet on his centre line well in front of his head, arms nearly straight, the right fist directly in line with his spine (not off beside his right shoulder). The knees are tucked toward the chest.
- Tick 45, follow-through: the somersault carries on to about 150 degrees (head below the hips, heading under him); the fists keep travelling round with the body, still together, and start to pull in toward his chest.
- Tick 54, the tuck: about 240 degrees, compact: knees at the chest, the fists open toward a relaxed half curl just outside his shins (beside them, a couple of centimetres clear, never touching the shins or feet), head tucked. He spins through.
- Tick 66: about 330 degrees, nearly upright, legs opening down under him, arms opening out low and wide.
- Tick 72: upright again (one full turn), close to the fall pose, still settling.
- Tick 84: balanced and close to the fall pose; from here the player can act.
- Tick 96: the fall pose, matching tick 0.

The somersault pitches the whole body forward (head going forward and down, feet going back and up) one full turn, 360 degrees, about his right-left axis, turning about his belly so he spins in place.

Flow. The hips lead every change of direction; the chest trails 1-3 ticks, the head and arms trail more, so the load and the strike are a wave travelling from the hips out to the fists. The big poses are moving holds, never frozen: across ticks 22-31 the fists keep rising 3-6 cm while the chest keeps arching, and the somersault never pauses between ticks 31 and 72. The head settles 1-2 ticks after the chest at the strike. The fists close a little tighter on the strike (about 5-10 degrees more curl at the knuckles between ticks 35 and 39). The legs counter the arms on the load (back when the arms go up) and tuck with the spin.

Tail: do not animate Tail1..5. The game's spring drives it from the body's motion, so the arch and the whip are what make it swing.

After the hit, the recovery is plain: the somersault completes, the body rebalances and the arms take the shortest calm path back to the fall pose. No gesture, no flourish in the ending.

Owner decisions on the approved key poses (2026-11-01). Take B and its key poses are approved; keep them. The game plays this 96-tick clip over a 48-tick stage (2x): hitbox live from game tick 16 for 7 ticks (clip 32-45), act from game tick 42, landing lag 12. Keep the fists on his centre line at the strike, even though his head hides them from straight behind at that instant; the hit effect marks the impact, so do not move the fists sideways to show them. No fist swell: both hands stay at normal scale for the whole clip, with every deform, offset and stretch helper at rest. The somersault is the hammer's momentum carrying through: keep it one clean, committed turn with no extra gestures, landing upright on his fall pose by the end. Fix the hands brushing his shins and feet in the tuck (ticks 45-60): keep both hands clear of the legs through the whole tuck.
